security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel reads sip.STIP as a hardware timer interrupt signal while menvcfg.STCE=0 and stimecmp is implemented. In this state, STIP in mip (and thus sip) is writable by M-mode firmware — not read-only as previously assumed — so a set STIP bit may originate from an M-mode write rather than from an stimecmp hardware comparison.
security_spec.summary: STIP in sip/mip is only hardware-gated when both stimecmp exists AND STCE=1; kernel timer ISR that trusts sip.STIP without correlating STCE state risks acting on M-mode-injected spurious interrupts

findings.finding: Timer ISR does NOT read CSR_SIP/STIP. Interrupt is dispatched via the generic IRQ domain from scause (hardware trap cause), not by polling sip. The handler clears the condition by writing ULONG_MAX to STIMECMP (or SBI call), never by clearing STIP in sip.

Interrupt dispatch reads scause (via pt_regs->cause) to determine interrupt source, then dispatches via generic_handle_domain_irq(). No sip polling — the hardware trap mechanism inherently delivers the correct cause number. A spurious STIP bit written by M-mode firmware cannot trigger this path unless accompanied by an actual trap with cause=IRQ_S_TIMER.

Trap entry reads CSR_CAUSE (scause) to distinguish interrupts from exceptions. The MSB of scause signals interrupt vs. exception; the cause number identifies timer interrupt. sip is never read on this path — a spurious STIP bit in sip cannot cause a spurious timer interrupt dispatch.
findings.snippet:
bge s4, zero, 1f
	/* Handle interrupts */
	call do_irq
	j ret_from_exception

findings.finding: Explicitly documents awareness that SIP is set by M-mode firmware (not directly by hardware), and intentionally omits SIP from save/restore. This shows design understanding that SIP is managed by M-mode. STIMECMP is saved/restored separately when SSTC is available.
findings.snippet:
/*
 * No need to save/restore IP CSR (i.e. MIP or SIP) because:
 * ...
 * 2. For MMU (S-mode) kernel, the bits in SIP are set by
 *    M-mode firmware and external devices (such as interrupt
 *    controller, etc).
 */

findings.finding: KVM VCPU timer save/restore operates on vstimecmp only, not on sip/hvip.STIP. Guest timer interrupts are managed via kvm_riscv_vcpu_set_interrupt() → hstatus/hvip writes. sip is never read for timer interrupt detection in the KVM path.

Timer stop clears the condition by writing ULONG_MAX to STIMECMP (with SSTC) or calling sbi_set_timer(U64_MAX) (without SSTC). It never clears STIP in sip. This is correct per RISC-V spec: stimecmp comparison is the root cause; clearing sip.STIP directly would be fragile and incomplete.

Only SIP write in the operational kernel is clearing IE_SIE (software interrupt) in sip after IPI handling — this is a software-generated interrupt bit that is explicitly set by S-mode itself via SBI, not subject to the STCE/STIP concern.
